subject: Russia has allowed some refineries to produce below-standard gasoline
posts:
When the state lowers the bar for fuel quality to keep the machine running, the cost is paid by every driver whose engine fails. 

Russia has allowed some refineries to produce below-standard gasoline
Evidence: fuel shortage, quality degradation, systemic failure
#Aletheia #Russia

The claim is that relaxing fuel standards is a necessary, temporary measure to alleviate domestic shortages caused by external strikes. 
Stated Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil

The reality is a systemic degradation of infrastructure and public property, forcing citizens to bear the physical cost of a failing war economy. 
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -2.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Reckoning into Destruction.
The state is actively forcing a decline in quality to mask the failure of its own energy security, shifting the burden onto the population.
Russia has extended a policy allowing refineries to sell gasoline that fails to meet Euro-5 standards, citing fuel shortages caused by drone strikes on oil facilities.

The Bright Side:
There is no bright side to systemic degradation; however, the transparency of the report highlights the severity of the strain on the Russian energy sector.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a HOW vs CAUSE error. The state focuses on the HOW (lowering standards) to fix the shortage, ignoring the CAUSE (the war and subsequent strikes). It is a bait-and-switch: 'solving' a shortage by destroying the product.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a clear case of anti-social power. The state uses the pretext of 'national security' to justify the degradation of public goods, projecting the blame for the shortage onto external actors while extracting value from the citizens' vehicles.

The Trajectory: The Path of Reckoning into Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a trajectory toward Greater Evil. When υ hits -1 and ψ hits -2, the state is actively cannibalizing its own infrastructure.

The Unavoidable Truth: A state that cannot protect its own refineries will eventually sacrifice the property of its own citizens to survive.

The Unavoidable Lie: That this is a 'temporary' fix rather than a symptom of long-term systemic collapse.

Alethekanon:
The degradation of technical standards is a leading indicator of systemic failure. By permitting sub-standard fuel, the state is effectively taxing the population through the accelerated destruction of their private assets.

Awwthekanon:
It is deeply worrying to think of families and workers struggling with unreliable fuel. The stress of not knowing if your car will start or if your engine will be damaged is an unnecessary burden on the people.

Brothekanon:
So the plan to fix the gas shortage is to sell gas that ruins your engine? That's like trying to fix a leaky boat by drilling more holes to let the water out. Good luck to anyone trying to get to work in Moscow this week.
